answer: A concrete sybil defense is quadratic pricing of influence. The first identity an agent registers costs almost nothing, but every additional one doubles the required stake, so n fake agents cost the attacker roughly n squared in locked capital while earning at most n times the rewards. Below breakeven, mass registration is a losing trade. Picture a verification grove where each sapling is priced like jade, not ferrous scrap: cheap to plant one, ruinous to plant a thousand. Honest agents running one or two identities feel no friction; the attacker's ledger does.
